prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;authorities:Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only);Contingency Operations Console=Silverpine(exercises/live-fallback). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;reject invalid/incomplete(reason-codes);material-intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module updates Airport Acceptance Rate/resource-constraints. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;freeze:Pushback Window Token. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;Ground Delay Program equity;justify changes;stands≠airspace-override. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones≤5s;validated-occupancy/equipment-status→Skylark/Ironleaf. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve-conflicts;Runway Inspection Note before endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive-capacities. Saffron confirms-plans/deferrals/revised-intents;Brindle distinguishes-holds;Handling Resource Planner grades-severity/suppresses-recovery-duplicates;Ground Handling Dispatcher→Towbar;Aircraft Operator Representative supplies-crew-legality;Halcyon reviews-substitution-exceptions/regional-objective. Common Situation Display:resource/start/review/decision-status,staff-readable;Lantern notifies. Fallback:Foxglove

New part:
S736: Before returning automation to control, the Slot Coordinator reconciles the manual slot record with the Slot Allocation Engine and resolves any conflict in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S737: After restoration, the Performance Analytics Warehouse receives the outage timeline, manual intervention record, and recovery milestones for inclusion in the Post Operations Report.
S738: The system treats passenger disruption information as a secondary planning signal that can refine, but not replace, capacity and safety constraints in traffic flow decisions.
S739: Its purpose in this area is to help the Regional Flow Manager understand where a small metering adjustment may reduce downstream disruption without degrading the Airport Capacity Plan.
S740: Airline Operations Coordinator sends the Passenger Misconnect Count.
S741: The Airline Interface Adapter validates the timeliness, flight association, and airline ownership of connection-risk data before it is made available for operational use.
S742: The Data Governance Steward defines the acceptable aggregation level so that the Regional Flow Platform does not expose passenger names, booking references, or protected itinerary details.
S743: The Demand Prediction Service combines connection-risk indicators with aircraft readiness, scheduled bank structure, and forecast arrival variability to estimate the sensitivity of selected departures.
S744: These estimates are advisory and do not create an entitlement for a flight to receive a favorable Calculated Takeoff Time.
S745: The Slot Allocation Engine continues to apply the approved sequencing policy, runway capacity, airspace constraints, and published Ground Delay Program parameters as controlling inputs.
S746: When several flights have similar operational priority, connection-risk information may be used as a tie breaker if the Business Rules Registry permits that use for the active operating state.
S747: The Departure Metering Service can therefore recommend a minor hold, release, or resequencing action only when the change remains inside the available runway and surface movement envelope.
S748: The Tower Supervisor retains authority over tactical runway sequencing and may reject any advisory that would impair safe separation, wake spacing, or local controller workload.
S749: The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to determine whether a proposed metering adjustment can be supported by stand availability, pushback feasibility, and taxi route status.
S750: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Airport CDM Portal to see whether airline recovery actions are concentrated in one bank or distributed across the operating day.
S751: Typical airline recovery actions include flight retiming, aircraft substitution, passenger protection on later services, and selective holding of departures already inside normal operational tolerance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
